By Nathan Layne
DEARBORN, Michigan, Nov 4 (Reuters) – The US president repeatedly branded him a jihadist. His Republican opponent questioned his loyalty to America. Campaign mailers suggested he had ties to terrorists and warned that, if elected, he would bring sharia law to Michigan.

Before Abdul El-Sayed could make history as the first Muslim elected to the US Senate, he endured what critics called one of the most overtly Islamophobic campaigns in modern US politics.

He won anyway. El-Sayed cast his victory in Tuesday’s midterm elections as a rebuke to such rhetoric, accusing his Republican opponent Mike Rogers of running what he called a historically ugly, hate-based campaign.

Show Full Article

“You chose hate, and Michigan chose hope,” El-Sayed said in his victory speech.

The attacks were a defining feature of the race, stirring safety concerns among residents in and around Dearborn, home to one of the nation’s largest Arab American communities, local officials and residents said this week.

El-Sayed, 42, a Michigan-born Egyptian American who has a medical degree and formerly served as Detroit’s health director, ran as a progressive focused on healthcare and the cost of living.

David Kolar, a 32-year-old music teacher, said the focus on El-Sayed’s faith recalled the backlash Muslims faced after the September 11, 2001, attacks, a period he believed the country had left behind.

“We have freedom of religion, and if he is of the Muslim faith, so be it,” Kolar said after casting his ballot for El-Sayed in the Detroit suburb of Warren.

Rogers said his objections to El-Sayed were ideological, not religious. Yet he portrayed him as a national security threat and campaigned alongside Republicans who went further.

Foremost among them was President Donald Trump, who labeled El-Sayed a terrorist and compared him to the September 11 hijackers. Rogers appeared with Senator John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican who said El-Sayed sleeps “in a bin Laden jersey,” and with Senator Ted Cruz, a Texas Republican, when he called El-Sayed a “jihadist leprechaun” and warned Americans would die if he won.

The attacks stood out not only for their severity but for how readily prominent Republicans embraced them, said Nazita Lajevardi, an associate professor at the University of Michigan who studies the intersection of politics, race and religion.

Unlike after September 11 or during Trump’s first-term Muslim ban, she said, there was little pushback from Republican party elites.

“This is the most egregious and most bigoted Islamophobic campaign I have seen,” she said. “What you’re seeing is not just hostility, racism and bigotry from the president … but you’re seeing it from rank-and-file members of the Republican Party.”

ANATOMY OF AN ATTACK CAMPAIGN

Led by Trump, Republicans portrayed Democratic candidates as radical, un-American and even communist throughout the campaign. Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico was derided in Texas as “Talafreako” over his views on gender and sexuality. In Ohio, ads weaponized Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton’s account of surviving sexual assault in her youth.

Voters appeared far more concerned with pocketbook issues than attacks, however, in an election season when Democrats, including Talarico and Acton, chalked up sweeping wins.

Still, perhaps no campaign leaned into identity politics as heavily as the Michigan Senate race.

Republicans sought to link El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood using decade-old writings on political change in Egypt and social media posts by his half-sister. The United States designated some Brotherhood branches as terrorist organizations this year. El-Sayed disavowed the group and denied any association, and no evidence has emerged linking him to it.

Republicans also seized on El-Sayed’s response to the March attack on Michigan’s Temple Israel synagogue. In a statement denouncing the violence, he said “hurt people hurt people,” drawing anger from some Jewish leaders who criticized the remark as rationalizing antisemitic violence.

He later apologized, saying that his comments may have been misconstrued and that “it wasn’t the time for context.”

Rogers’ allies invoked the episode through the campaign’s final hours. On the eve of the election, the Michigan Republican Party held a press conference featuring Jewish and Black community leaders opposed to El-Sayed beside a large red sign accusing him of offering “SAFE HARBOR TO TERRORISTS.”

Asked by Reuters to substantiate the claim, party communications director Ted Goodman pointed to the “hurt people hurt people” remark, which he said amounted to justifying a terrorist attack against children.

The argument resonated with some voters. Five of roughly 30 people Reuters interviewed in the Detroit area said El-Sayed’s Muslim faith or perceived links to extremism strongly influenced their vote for Rogers.

Robin Cook, 73, was one of them. “I don’t think he’s a true American,” he said of El-Sayed. “I don’t trust him.”

DEARBORN PUSHES BACK

Most voters interviewed dismissed the attacks as desperate and a distraction from their economic concerns. Non-Muslims stressed that Muslims and Arab Americans were woven into their daily lives, pointing to friends, neighbors, colleagues and physicians in their communities.

“I grew up around all nationalities,” said Pamela Johnson, a 72-year-old Catholic, after voting for El-Sayed. “We all matter, regardless of color, race or whatever.”

But Dearborn residents said the rhetoric carried real-world consequences, fueling safety fears.

Imad Soofi, a business owner who immigrated from Yemen two decades ago, said he had seen a rise in anti-Muslim hostility since Trump began targeting El-Sayed, including remarks directed at women wearing hijabs in public.

A three-time Trump voter, Soofi, 49, said he might have backed Rogers had the candidate distanced himself from Trump’s anti-Muslim rhetoric. Instead, he voted for El-Sayed.

Alabas Farhat, who represents parts of Dearborn and Detroit in the Michigan House, said the campaign recycled anti-Muslim tropes Arab Americans in the region had encountered for years.

“There has been this constant questioning of how American can you be as a Muslim? How American can you be as an Arab American?” Farhat said in an interview. “It happens, but time and again, we show how American we are.”

(Reporting by Nathan Layne in Dearborn, Detroit, Warren, and Harrison Township, Michigan; editing by Paul Thomasch and Howard Goller)

FAST

Nov 4 : Federico Valverde struck in stoppage time to give Real Madrid a dramatic 3-2 Champions League victory at AEK Athens on Wednesday, while Liverpool surrendered the lead twice in a 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce.
Real twice came from behind to maintain their perfect start and sit second on 12 points from four matches, behind Paris St Germain on goal difference.
AEK threatened from the outset and their early pressure was rewarded in the 12th minute when Aboubakary Koita cut inside and fired into the top corner from just inside the box.
Thibaut Courtois denied Luka Jovic before Jude Bellingham, who had an effort ruled out for offside in the 27th minute, equalised five minutes later with a deft backheel from Marc Cucurella's low cross.

Koita's driving run and pass set up Stavros Pilios to restore AEK's lead in the 75th minute, his low shot going through Courtois' legs.
Kylian Mbappe tapped in Denzel Dumfries' cross three minutes later before Valverde delivered the winner, leaving AEK 30th on three points.
LIVERPOOL'S WINNING START ENDS
Liverpool arrived in Istanbul with three wins from three but Vedat Muriqi's 79th-minute winner ended that run and earned Fenerbahce their first victory of the campaign.
Trey Nyoni opened the scoring in the 25th minute, meeting a defensive header with a low volley that deflected off Kojo Peprah Oppong and wrongfooted Ederson.
Mason Greenwood levelled four minutes later with a free kick that was heading wide before striking Jeremy Jacquet in the defensive wall and skidding past Alisson.
Substitutes Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak combined to restore Liverpool's lead in the 69th minute. Gakpo exchanged passes with Kostas Tsimikas before reaching the byline and delivering a cross for Isak to power a close-range header past Ederson.
The advantage lasted four minutes. Following a short corner, N'Golo Kante crossed and Gakpo's glancing header diverted the ball away from Alisson, leaving Archie Brown to tap into an unguarded net at the far post.
Brown then supplied the winner, looping the ball into the box after a long throw was headed back to him. Surrounded by three Liverpool defenders, Muriqi somehow headed past Alisson, wrapping up a poor night for Liverpool's defence.
Andoni Iraola's side dropped to fifth with nine points, while Fenerbahce climbed to 19th on five.

Source: Reuters

US President Donald Trump said the war was necessary to stop Iran from “having a nuclear weapon” and added that he “would have done nothing different”.

WASHINGTON: US P resident Donald Trump said on Wednesday (Nov 4) the Iran war has been worth it despite acknowledging its role in losses in US midterm elections in which his Republican party lost control of Congress.
"The Iran thing we had to do, and we continue to do it," he told reporters.
T he Iran war was responsible for a spike in gasoline prices that were seen as a strong factor in why Democrats made big gains in the elections.
T rump said the war has been worth it to stop Tehran from "having a nuclear weapon."

He said he was okay with Vice President JD Vance's social media post earlier on Wednesday in which Vance referred to deep electoral losses and said "the reason we lost is the war."
"I can tell you that as far as that war is concerned, I would have done nothing different," Trump said.
Trump also again said that if he had been on the ballot, he believed "we would have won."
"But they just, you couldn't transfer that love. There was such love at those rallies, it was incredible and we weren't able to transfer the love to candidates," he said.

items.title: Oil prices plunge 10% as US midterm results raise hopes of Iran war's end
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: Brent crude plunged 10 per cent to a two-month low as investors bet that Democratic gains in the US midterm elections could accelerate efforts to end the Iran war and ease oil supply pressures ...
items.body: By Mia Gindis, Charles Gorrivan and Grant Smith Brent oil futures plunged 10 per cent to trade below $100 a barrel as investors wagered that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could usher in a quicker end to the months-long Iran conflict that upended global energy markets. The global benchmark slumped to a session low of $93.22 a barrel, the lowest in two months, as traders digested the results of an election that was largely seen as a referendum on affordability and a war that’s deeply unpopular at home. West Texas Intermediate, meanwhile, plummeted below $90. Wednesday’s declines also triggered selling from trend-following commodity trading advisers. Prices took a fresh lunge lower after Vice-President JD Vance directly attributed Republican losses to the overseas conflict. Investors recalibrated positions to account for a sooner-than-anticipated wind-down, with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer pledging to end the war, saying some Republicans would back the effort. Any progress towards a resolution could further boost flows through the vital Strait of Hormuz. US President Donald Trump, for his part, told the Financial Times he had no immediate plans to ramp up fighting in West Asia. Gas prices averaged over $4 a gallon as Americans cast their ballots on Tuesday, exceeding that level on an election day for the first time on record. “With this election result and Iran’s economic situation, it does seem like a deal is more likely than not,” said Ajay Parmar, director of energy at ICIS. “Trump’s strength is reduced considerably.” Technical factors also amplified oil’s sell-off. Trend-following commodity trading advisers slashed long positions to about 55 per cent in Brent from 73 per cent at the start of the session, according to data from Kpler’s Bridgeton Research Group. The robot traders are known for a tendency to exacerbate price swings. The election could serve as an inflection point in a war that had no immediate end in sight and has roiled West Asian energy flows, pushing oil up about 50 per cent this year. The squeeze on Persian Gulf supplies, along with escalating Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, has also driven up fuel prices. Data from the US Energy Information Administration showed that domestic diesel stockpiles were below 100 million barrels for the first time since 2003, indicating that a ceasefire would bring little immediate relief to an exceptionally tight global market. In crude oil markets, however, physical market prices have generally weakened recently, with flows through Hormuz holding near pre-war levels. West Asian oil metrics indicate near-term supply is outpacing demand for the first time since July, while prices for North Sea cargoes have also eased. Time spreads for both benchmarks also weakened broadly, with several narrowing to their lowest levels since mid-October. JPMorgan Chase & Co. said in a report that global oil markets had returned to a surplus as a result of the West Asian rebound, with an overhang of 1.4 million barrels a day in October. Saudi Aramco will maximise oil production this quarter as it boosts shipments from near pre-war levels seen in October, Chief Executive Officer Amin Nasser said in a post-earnings call on Tuesday. The United Arab Emirates is considering a third oil-export pipeline that will deliver crude outside Hormuz, according to people familiar with the matter. “With both chambers now capable of passing resolutions, holding back war funding and delaying confirmations, the administration faces a shorter political runway and greater institutional pressure to find a Hormuz deal,” said Claudio Galimberti, chief economist at Rystad Energy.

DUBLIN, Nov 4 : Ireland coach Andy Farrell challenged his surprise selections to grab their opportunity after making changes to the side to take on Argentina in the Nations Championship on Friday.
Scrumhalf Craig Casey was chosen ahead of Jamison Gibson-Park in Farrell's side for the test in Dublin. Former World Rugby Player of the Year Josh van der Flier was replaced in the starting lineup by Nick Timoney as the Ireland coach seeks to widen the selection pool with the 2027 World Cup in Australia less than a year away.
“Craig deserves to play in a big game at the start of the season, to have the responsibility to be in charge of the week and take responsibility for how we play on Friday,” he told a press conference on Wednesday after naming his line-up.
“We need him to be able to have the opportunity to do that. Plus he’s been playing pretty well himself. He knows the competition is there but he’s got the shirt so it’s up to him to make a good first impression.”

Timoney will be the openside flank. “Certainly last year he grabbed hold of the understanding of what he can bring and what international rugby is all about,” Farrell said of the 31-year-old Ulster loose forward, who made his test debut five years ago.
“We saw a consistency within that. He brings a lot not just to our game but in different positions as well. Nick gets to wear the seven jersey for the first game and I’m sure Josh will have something to say about that in the coming weeks as well.”
Ireland take on Fiji next weekend where Farrell is expected to give opportunities to others on the fringes of selection. 
“You have to keep them hungry as well,” he said of squad players. “They will stay hungry no matter what, because that’s the type of people that they are, but you’ve got to make sure your squad is your strength, certainly for what’s coming up in the next 12 months. It’s important that we keep feeding that.
“If ever a player feels comfortable, we’re failing the group, but we’ve not got those players anyway. I don’t think people are comfortable, just by their nature, but if you want to keep ambition growing as a group then you’ve got to keep the ambition within the individual,” Farrell added.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

items.title: Democrats’ Senate win could shield Federal Reserve from Trump’s influence, but risks persist
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: Democrats’ midterm victory could strengthen the Federal Reserve’s independence by limiting President Donald Trump’s ability to appoint allies to its board. A Democrat controlled Senate could also intensify scrutiny of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, with Elizabeth Warren likely to lead the Senate Banking Committee and challenge the administration’s banking reforms.
items.body: Democrats’ sweeping midterm victory could strengthen the Federal Reserve’s ability to resist President Donald Trump’s attempts to influence monetary policy, with their expected control of the Senate emerging as a key obstacle to his efforts to reshape the central bank, Reuters reported.Control of the upper chamber gives Democrats significant leverage over Fed appointments, potentially making it harder for Trump to install allies on the central bank’s seven member board. However, the political shift could also bring greater scrutiny of Chairman Kevin Warsh and complicate the administration’s efforts to overhaul banking regulations.For live updates on US Markets, click here Senate control puts Trump’s Fed appointments under pressureThe change in political balance could significantly limit Trump’s ability to influence the Fed through appointments. Three of the central bank’s seven governors were appointed by former President Joe Biden, while former Chair Jerome Powell remains on the board despite his growing differences with Trump.Also Read: US stocks rally after Democrats' midterm sweep as AI infrastructure stocks slideTrump has repeatedly criticised the current composition of the board, calling it hostile and partisan , while pressing policymakers to cut interest rates. The Fed, however, has prioritised controlling inflation, Reuters reported.The Senate’s role in confirming nominees could become particularly important if Trump succeeds in removing Governor Lisa Cook. His administration is expected to pursue an administrative procedure in the coming weeks to establish grounds for her dismissal over alleged errors in mortgage applications filed before she joined the Fed.Cook is likely to challenge any removal in court. Even if Trump succeeds, a Democrat controlled Senate would make it difficult for him to secure confirmation of a replacement.Warsh faces tougher scrutiny as Warren gains influenceThe political shift could also make Warsh’s position more challenging. Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren is likely to take charge of the Senate Banking Committee, replacing Republican Tim Scott, a Trump ally and supporter of Warsh.Warren has been a vocal critic of Warsh and could intensify scrutiny of his financial disclosures, including his handling of hundreds of millions of dollars in assets before taking the Fed’s top job.Democrats could also question his approach to inflation and monetary policy, particularly after campaigning heavily on the cost of living.Economists at Monetary Policy Analytics said Warsh got no support for his chairmanship from Democrats... Hostile questioning could put Warsh's rhetoric to the test .Meanwhile, Democratic control of key congressional committees could slow banking and regulatory changes backed by the administration and Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman, including stablecoin rules under the Genius Act and changes to the Fed's bank supervision framework, Reuters reported.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

Nov 4 : Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell said on Wednesday that he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress on upper-body movement after he was carried off the field during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. 
Campbell, 26, lay motionless on the ground after making a hit on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson in the fourth quarter at Ford Field before being taken to hospital.
The Lions said on Monday that preliminary indications were positive.
"I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time," Campbell, a Detroit captain this season, said in a statement.

items.title: トランプ氏「イラン戦争が共和党に打撃」、 熱狂的支持を候補者に波及できず
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は４日、対イラン戦争が共和党の中間選挙での敗北の一因になったと認めながらも、戦争には価値があったとの考えを示した。

トランプ氏は記者団に対し「イランの件はやらなければならなかったし、今後も続けていく」と述べ、イランが核兵器を保有するのを阻止するために戦争は価値があったと主張した。

３日投開票の中間選挙では民主党が連邦議会上下両院の過半数を奪還。対イラン戦争を受けてガソリン価格が上昇したことが野党・民主党の大幅な議席増につながった要因の１つと受け止められている。

こうした中、バンス副大統領はこの日、「われわれが（中間選挙で）敗北した理由は戦争だ」とし、「それでも、戦争には価値があった、今後６年間にわたり上院（の多数派）を失う代償を払うだけの価値があったと主張したいなら、そうすればいい」とＸに投稿。トランプ大統領が進めた対イラン戦争との距離を置く姿勢を示し、有権者の厳しい審判は全面的にイラン戦争に原因があったとの認識を示した。

トランプ氏はこれについて問題視しない考えを示し、「その戦争について言えば、私なら違う対応はしなかった」と述べた。また、自分自身が中間選挙の投票対象だったら勝利していたと改めて主張。「選挙集会では信じられないほどの熱狂と支持があったが、その支持を候補者たちに移し替えることはできなかった」と語った。

FAST

Nov 4 : American goalie Connor Hellebuyck said "challenging circumstances involving my family" led him to request a trade from the Winnipeg Jets, addressing fans in a letter on Wednesday ahead of his return to the Canadian city.
Hellebuyck, a three-time Vezina Trophy winner as the NHL's top goalie who also helped the US beat Canada in the gold medal game at the 2026 Olympics, sat out training camp and missed the opening weeks of the 2026-27 season before being sent to the New Jersey Devils in a blockbuster trade less than two weeks ago.
"I know my decision to request a trade was disappointing and frustrating for many people, especially those who supported me throughout my career,” Hellebuyck wrote on Instagram ahead of the Devils' game at Winnipeg next Tuesday. 
“I understand those feelings, and I want everyone to know it was an extremely difficult decision.”

Hellebuyck publicly confirmed in August that he wanted to leave Winnipeg, saying at the time that he had requested a move "several months ago".
After helping the United States win Olympic gold, Hellebuyck and a number of his US teammates attended a White House reception hosted by President Donald Trump, who announced that the goalie would be awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
The 33-year-old Hellebuyck, who holds the Jets franchise’s record for most wins (345) and shutouts (45), faced a backlash in Canada for the White House visit and said in March that while he could handle the criticism he was upset his wife had borne the brunt of it.
Hellebuyck, who is off to a 3-0 start with the Devils, thanked the entire Jets organization and the team's fans while also stopping short of divulging further details about his decision to seek a trade.
“There were several considerations that went into my decision, including some very challenging circumstances involving my family,” Hellebuyck wrote. “After a lot of thought and discussion, we ultimately felt that making a change was the best thing for our family.
"We've chosen to keep those personal circumstances private, and I hope people can respect that."

Source: Reuters

items.title: バンス副大統領、共和党敗北は「イラン戦争が原因」 トランプ氏と一線
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Phil Stewart

[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Phil Stewart

[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - バンス米副大統領は４日、Ｘへの投稿で、トランプ大統領が進めた対イラン戦争との距離を置く姿勢を示し、その意義に疑問を呈するとともに、中間選挙で野党・民主党に議会支配を許した有権者の厳しい審判は全面的にイラン戦争に原因があったとの認識を示した。

バンス氏は「われわれが（中間選挙で）敗北した理由は戦争だ」とし、「それでも、戦争には価値があった、今後６年間にわたり上院（の多数派）を失う代償を払うだけの価値があったと主張したいなら、そうすればいい」とＸに投稿。過去に戦争終結を勧告したことについても「妥当な助言だった」とした。

３日投開票の中間選挙では、民主党が連邦議会上下両院の過半数を奪還。共和党の牙城にも食い込んで幅広い勝利を収め、有権者がトランプ大統領に厳しい審判を下した形となった。トランプ大統領が対イラン大規模軍事作戦の再開を検討する中、バンス氏が中間選挙の翌日にこうした異例の投稿を行ったことで、政権の判断が一段と複雑になる可能性がある。

この発言は国防総省高官、とりわけヘグセス国防長官の政治的立場にも疑問を投げかける。トランプ氏はヘグセス氏について、早い段階から戦争を支持していたと説明している。ヘグセス氏は議員からも厳しい批判を浴びている。

２０２４年の大統領選でトランプ氏を２期目に押し上げた保守地盤の有権者も民主党側へ大きく傾いた。背景には対イラン戦争への強い不満に加え、高止まりする生活費への不安など、トランプ政権の国政運営に対する不満があると見られる。

バンス氏はトランプ氏との見解の相違を小さく見せようと努め、トランプ氏自身もイラン戦争が中間選挙での共和党敗北の一因だったと認めていると指摘。ただ、トランプ氏の発言はより抑制的で、イラン戦争は敗因の１つにすぎないとの見方を示している。

トランプ氏はバンス氏の発言について記者団に問われ、良い発言だったとの考えを示し、「彼がどう感じているかは分かっている」と述べた。一方で、「われわれはイランによる核兵器の保有を阻止した」と述べ、戦争を擁護した。

ホワイトハウス顧問はロイターに対し、一部の当局者や職員はバンス氏の投稿を、外交政策を巡って大統領との一線を画し、戦争が国内経済に影響を及ぼしたと公に認めるものと受け止めたと語った。

＜２８年大統領選＞

バンス氏は、２０２８年大統領選の有力候補と目されている。バンス氏の対抗馬となる可能性があるルビオ国務長官は、中間選挙以降、沈黙を守っている。

事情に詳しい人物は、バンス氏の発言は２８年大統領選に向けた選挙運動の始まりと受け止めることもできると述べた。

ホワイトハウスの一部当局者は、バンス氏の投稿について事前に知らされていたと述べた。ただ、ホワイトハウス当局者の１人はロイターの質問に対し、ホワイトハウスの高官は、全員とは言わないまでも大半が不意を突かれたと述べた。

選挙後にイラン戦争が再燃するとの懸念がある中、仲介者らは終結に向けた取り組みを強めている。

バンス氏はここ数週間、イラン政府との交渉に一段と力を入れている。ただ、イラン側には、ウラン濃縮度をゼロに引き下げることなど、米国の要求を受け入れる意向を示す動きはほとんどない。

FAST

Nov 4 : Rory McIlroy backed criticism of LIV Golf on Wednesday, saying the Saudi-backed breakaway league had taken players and sponsors from rival tours and turned professional golf into an "arms race".
McIlroy said he agreed with DP World Tour Chief Executive Guy Kinnings' assertion that LIV had sought to undermine the European circuit, pointing to comments made by people involved with the league at this year's Masters about wanting to destroy the tour.
"They took players; they took sponsors; they turned professional golf into an arms race," the Northern Irishman told reporters ahead of the Abu Dhabi Championship.
"They were going around Augusta saying they wanted to destroy The European Tour. Yeah, I agree with everything."

McIlroy acknowledged that LIV's investment had brought benefits, including the creation of the International Series on the Asian Tour, but said the latter had ultimately been left without the support it needed.
"Where did that leave the Asian Tour? They left them high and dry," he said, adding that the tour had since returned to the fold through partnerships with the PGA Tour and DP World Tour.
The six-times major champion said LIV's financial model was always likely to face difficulties if investors failed to see a return or decided to redirect their money elsewhere.
Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, which has invested more than $5 billion in LIV since its launch in 2022, is ending its financial backing after the 2026 season.
LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September and has secured a proposed financing commitment of up to $300 million from BC Partners Credit as it seeks to restructure ahead of 2027.
McIlroy, 37, added the disruption caused by the breakaway league could ultimately leave men's golf on a more sustainable footing.
"For long-term sustainability for men's professional golf, I think we are in a much better spot," he said.

items.title: ロ通販大手オゾン物流拠点で火災、ウクライナのドローン攻撃受け
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[４日 ロイター] - ウクライナによるドローン（無人機）攻撃により、ロシア南部のアディゲ共和国アディゲイスクにある電子商取引大手オゾンの物流拠点で火災が発生した。同社と地域当局者が４日明らかにした。

アディゲイスクにあるオゾンの施設が標的とされたのは今回が２回目となる。ウクライナは７月以降、ロシアの経済と戦争遂行能力に打撃を与えるため、同社および競合他社のワイルドベリーズが運営する数十カ所の巨大倉庫を攻撃しており、今回はその一連の攻撃の一環とみられる。

ロシアもウクライナの商業施設に対して同様の攻撃を行っており、地上戦線の状況が概ね膠着状態にある一方で、ここ数カ月、双方が空戦を激化させている。米国の仲介で１１月１０─１１日にアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）のアブダビで行われる和平協議を前に、ロシアは３日、ウクライナのエネルギーインフラに対し複数回にわたる大規模な波状攻撃を実施。ウクライナも２日、中部ヤロスラブリの石油精製施設を攻撃した。 

オゾンは、今回の攻撃による死傷者は確認されておらず、施設の従業員は全員避難したと述べた。今回の攻撃に先立ち、オゾンは先週発表した決算で、１１カ所の施設へのドローン攻撃により３０１億ルーブル（３億６７００万ドル）の損失が発生する見込みだと明らかにしていた。

items.title: ＥＣＢ総裁、気候変動対策呼びかけ　ＣＯＰ３１首脳会議にらみ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [フランクフルト ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[フランクフルト ４日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁は４日、欧州で夏の猛暑に伴う大きな被害が発生したことを踏まえ、気候変動関連の対策を強めるよう欧州連合（ＥＵ）に呼びかけた。国連気候変動枠組み条約第３１回締約国会議（ＣＯＰ３１）首脳会議が来週トルコで開かれるのを前にした発言で、関連した保険の整備や電力インフラへの投資拡大、企業による自家発電強化を挙げた。

ロイターが確認した内部文書によると、ＥＵはＣＯＰ３１首脳会議で、温室効果ガス排出削減に向けた「パッケージ」に関する合意をまとめたい考えだ。

ラガルド氏はブログで「夏の異常気象が常態化しつつある中、欧州は先を見据えて準備を進め、経済的損失を防ぐ必要がある」と述べた。熱波や山火事などで欧州の経済やエネルギー面で弱点が示されており、温暖化で問題が深刻化しかねないと主張した。

ラガルド氏は、欧州での災害損失のうち保険でカバーされてきたのは４分の１に過ぎないと指摘。気候災害に備えた官民共同の再保険の仕組みづくりの必要性を強調した。送電網を拡充する投資が全体としてのコスト削減につながるとしたほか、太陽光発電の活用に向けた蓄電能力の向上、自家発電設備の保有企業が需要ひっ迫の際に供給支援するようなルールづくりを提言した。

ラガルド氏は、民間部門からの多くの投資が必要だとし、資金調達面でのＥＣＢの施策については言及しなかった。ラガルド氏は来年２月７日に退任することを発表している。

FAST

HOUSTON/NEW YORK, Nov 4 : Texas' red-hot data center industry has been plunged into uncertainty by governor-elect Gina Hinojosa's pledge to crack down on the rapid growth of server warehouse projects.
Hinojosa, who ousted Republican Greg Abbott in a dramatic upset on Tuesday, hammered that message in the final weeks of her campaign, calling for a statewide moratorium and vowing days before the vote to “stop the data center takeover.”
With plentiful energy supplies, relatively cheap land and a pro-business policy, Texas has become one of the hottest regions for data center development in recent years. Big Tech companies including Meta, Google and Microsoft have announced major data center projects in the state over the past two years. 
But growing opposition from rural communities and a surge in requests to connect to the state’s power grid had pushed even the Republican governor, Abbott, to order a pause on data center permits earlier this year.

Before the election, Hinojosa said she would take the crackdown on data centers a step further by banning all data center approvals until the state legislature passes laws "to protect Texans, so that Texans have a seat at the table to decide if and how data centers come into our community."
The data center industry had already come under pressure before the midterms. On August 3, Abbott became one of the first Republican governors in the US to halt the connection of new data centers to the state's electric grid. He also ordered a comprehensive audit of the projects, with a focus on power demand, environmental impacts and tax breaks given to developers. 
The move represented a dramatic shift in Abbott's approach to data centers, which he had supported just months earlier. By the time Texas halted data centers connecting to its grid, state grid operator ERCOT said it was tracking more than 400 gigawatts of data center projects - roughly equivalent to what it would take to power the entire US South - seeking to connect to the grid.
Abbott's about-face also threw tens of billions of dollars of data center projects planned in Texas into jeopardy and raised doubts over whether hundreds of millions in grid deposits paid by data centers seeking to connect to the grid would be returned.
Since ordering the audit, Abbott has also taken actions to penalize data center water violations retroactively and temporarily banned the state from issuing air permits for the projects.
Abbott, however, did not issue a formal moratorium on data centers, which Hinojosa has vowed to do. Certain measures by Abbott also had a near-term expiration date, like the air permit ban and the audit, which was expected to conclude at the end of 2026.
“The data centers connect economic development to everyday concerns,” University of Houston political scientist Brandon Rottinghaus said a day before the vote, citing electricity bills, water supplies and property rights.
Polling showed rural voters, who are “at the epicenter of so many of these fights,” were unhappy with the spread of data centers heading into the election, he said.
Some 42 per cent of registered voters in a Reuters/Ipsos poll published this week said limiting the construction of data centers used to power AI was very important or the most important issue for them.
Some 76 per cent of voters nationwide said they opposed the construction of a new data center in their community, according to an NBC and SSRS exit poll. Ahead of the vote, a University of Houston poll in October found that 79 per cent of likely Texas voters supported limits on the number of data centers that can be built in the state.
"Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now," Elon Musk, who supported Abbott in the election and had spent $158 million to promote Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton alone, wrote early Wednesday on X. 

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 5 : Japan plans to seek earlier access to information on undisclosed software vulnerabilities from US artificial intelligence developers and other overseas technology firms as it moves to strengthen defences against rising cyberattacks, the Nikkei newspaper reported on Thursday.
The government is expected to present an emergency cybersecurity package at a ministerial meeting that could be convened as early as Friday, the report added.
In late October, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi instructed officials to devise steps to bolster cyber defences following a recent increase in cyberattacks, according to Nikkei.
Government and corporate websites in several countries were disrupted in October after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, prompting millions of hacking attempts and forcing website operators to protect or temporarily shut down their systems.

As organisations scrambled to mitigate PHP risks, Japan said it would set up a team to simulate cyberattacks using AI to identify weaknesses in technology systems.
Tokyo will now explore ways to obtain information about serious software vulnerabilities before they are publicly disclosed to help government agencies and operators of critical infrastructure respond more quickly, Nikkei said.
Japan had recently sought expanded access to advanced AI models from major US developers, including Anthropic and OpenAI, in response to a wave of cyberattacks believed to have been aided by AI, Nikkei added.

Nov 5 : Japan plans to seek earlier access to information on undisclosed software vulnerabilities from US artificial intelligence developers and other overseas technology firms as it moves to strengthen defences against rising cyberattacks, the Nikkei newspaper reported on Thursday.
The government is expected to present an emergency cybersecurity package at a ministerial meeting that could be convened as early as Friday, the report added.
In late October, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi instructed officials to devise steps to bolster cyber defences following a recent increase in cyberattacks, according to Nikkei.
Government and corporate websites in several countries were disrupted in October after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, prompting millions of hacking attempts and forcing website operators to protect or temporarily shut down their systems.

Nov 4 : Democrats' midterm election sweep sent shares in US tech giants soaring on Wednesday as investors bet that potential curbs on new data-center construction could cement their grip on scarce computing power while easing pressure on strained cash flows.
Shares of Amazon surged 7.4 per cent to a three-month high while Meta Platforms, Alphabet and Microsoft gained between 2 per cent and 6.3 per cent, powering a rally on Wall Street after days of selling fueled by fears over the AI boom's soaring costs.
Apple, which has avoided Big Tech's massive AI spending but is feeling the sting of an AI-fueled surge in memory chip prices, jumped nearly 7 per cent to a record high.
If the gains hold, the five companies are on course to add more than $750 billion in combined market value.

The rally marks a sharp reversal for the battered cloud giants after their quarterly earnings showed how the AI infrastructure race was turning once cash-rich, debt-light companies into heavy spenders reliant on borrowing. Microsoft was the notable exception, with $18.6 billion in cash flow.
The gains followed landslide midterm victories for Democrats who oppose data centers, including in Texas, likely accelerating a backlash against the power-hungry, water-intensive and noisy facilities that are at the heart of the AI boom but increasingly unpopular with local communities.
"Conceptually, post-election, there may be a bit of a slowdown or some bumps in the road for future data-center build-out," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth.
"The hyperscalers (large tech companies) already have data centers, so those assets are more valuable now because there's not going to be an overbuild of data centers. Also, if there's a slower pace of data-center build-out, then there's going to be a slower pace of CapEx spending. That certainly would impact the hyperscalers."
The tech giants have been building capacity at a blistering pace, with plans to spend more than $740 billion this year, up from roughly $400 billion last year. That far outstrips smaller AI cloud rivals such as CoreWeave and Nebius.
Shares of smaller players including Applied Digital and Iren plunged between 6 per cent and 13 per cent on fears that curbs on data-center construction could derail their debt-fueled expansion plans. The companies have been spending several times their revenue to meet a swelling backlog of orders.
"The biggest worry of the night for tech investors and the AI trade was around the state of Texas, where ~25 per cent-30 per cent of data-center gigawatts and capacity will come from," said Dan Ives, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives.
"Now it will happen at a more measured pace, which is likely a good thing in the eyes of many investors."

Source: Reuters

JERUSALEM: Benjamin Netanyahu 's political rivals seize d on Democrats' capture of the US Congress as proof that he had squandered generations of bipartisan American support for Israel, as they seek a chance to form a government without him.
Democrats won majorities in both the Senate and Ho us e in Tuesday's (Nov 3) midterm election, in a scathing rebuke to US President Donald Trump fuelled in part by deep fr us tration over the unpopular US -Israeli war on Iran.
The US vote took place j us t a week after an Israeli election, when Netanyahu 's right-wing coalition lost its parliamentary majority but performed well enough to deny his main opponent Gadi Eisenkot a clear path to unseat him.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog is due to hold talks on Wednesday and Thursday with party representatives before tasking one of the two men with forming the next government. Meanwhile Netanyahu remains prime minister as a caretaker.

US SUPPORT WAVERS FOR LONGSTANDING ALLY The United States has been Israel's staunchest ally for generations under presidents of both parties, providing billions of dollars a year in military aid since the 1970s. But unlike previo us leaders who assiduo us ly courted Democrats and Republicans alike, Netanyahu has openly backed Republicans.
Support for Israel among Democrats and some Republicans wavered after Israel launched its military assault in Gaza following the 2023 Hamas attack, and fell further t his year since Trump and Netanyahu ordered a joint attack on Iran.
Some Democratic candidates made criticism of American military aid to Israel a prominent campaign argument. On Tuesday, Trump, who had endorsed Netanyahu , made an election-day pledge to halt US$4 billion in annual funding to Israel, a move he said would take away a "bad talking point" us ed by Democrats.
Yair Golan, head of Israel's centre-left opposition Democrats party, said on X that the US midterm election results "reveal j us t how toxic Netanyahu is among both Democrats and Republicans".
Centrist opposition leader Yair Lapid said the results showed "Israel cannot afford" for Netanyahu to remain in office.
"It endangers our security, it jeopardises our democracy, and it will ruin our standing on the global stage," Lapid said in a social media post.

Netanyahu has so far remained silent about the outcome of the US vote. His office did not respond to a request for comment.
It could be weeks or months before it becomes clear whether it is Netanyahu or Eisenkot who ultimately faces the task of repairing the relationship. Whichever candidate is chosen first m us t build a new coalition or the other will be given an opportunity. If both fail, a new election would be called.
Meanwhile, Udi Sommer, a professor of political science at Tel Aviv University, predicted that the incoming Democratic-controlled US Congress would be the most adversarial towards Israel in its his tory.
Although most power over foreign policy still resides with the president, Democrats could apply pressure through hearings, congress ional oversight and budgetary measures, he said.
"The Democratic landslide and the Republican wipeout encapsulate the next chapter in US -Israel relations," Sommer said.

WASHINGTON, Nov 4 : The crypto industry's roughly $200 million spending spree this election stumbled Tuesday, as some of its most expensive and high-profile targets, including the Senate race in Ohio, did not go its way.
While the industry won most of the races it targeted, those losses raised questions among lobbyists about whether it had backed the right candidates. 
The greatest blow for the industry came in Ohio, where Democrat and crypto skeptic Sherrod Brown decisively won his race to return to the Senate, despite crypto political action committees spending more than $60 million to defeat him. 
The race was one of the most expensive in the Senate's history. Strategists viewed it as a major test of crypto's political clout after the Senate in September voted against advancing major crypto legislation known as the Clarity Act due to opposition from Democrats, in a blow for an industry that has grown close to President Donald Trump.

Some progressive Democratic primary candidates also successfully attacked opponents over their crypto ties.
"We see this as souring the political environment for crypto," said Jaret Seiberg, an analyst with TD Cowen, in a note on Tuesday.
The leading industry super PAC, Fairshake, notched one high-profile victory, as it and its affiliates spent at least $13.5 million to defeat Nebraska independent Senate candidate Dan Osborn, a former labor union leader. Osborn lost to Republican Senator Pete Ricketts, who voted for the Clarity Act. 
“As the biggest spender in the Nebraska Senate race, we’re proud to have helped Sen. Ricketts weather the waves of a hard-fought cycle," said Geoff Vetter, a spokesperson for Fairshake. 
Fairshake, whose chief backers include Coinbase, Ripple and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, threw its financial heft behind 32 House candidates — 19 Republicans and 13 Democrats — whom it considered supporters of the industry's priorities. 
So far, it has won 29 of the 34 races it spent on, with several races not yet called. Of the six House candidates on whom Fairshake spent $1 million or more, so far it has won three. 
"Newly elected and current members will have a choice: protect consumers and American jobs or fight progress," Fairshake's Vetter said.  
The crypto industry has spent roughly half a billion dollars over the past two election cycles to build a bipartisan coalition of congressional allies to advance its interests. 
In 2024, it helped elect dozens of crypto-friendly lawmakers who later came together to pass a law to help promote adoption of dollar-backed tokens known as stablecoins.
The Clarity Act's defeat was a major setback, and with Democrats taking Congress, the industry now faces oversight and potential investigations, particularly its ties to Trump. 
Cryptocurrencies posted overnight losses on the results, but recovered on Wednesday. Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency, was last up 3.1 per cent above $80,000. 
Crypto executives frequently say the long-term trend is still favorable.
"Where crypto is today compared to we were two years ago is night and day," said Stu Alderoty, chief legal officer at Ripple, speaking before the results. However, on the possibility of Democratic probes into Trump's crypto business dealings, he said: "I think the writing is on the wall.”

(Additional reporting by Dawn Kopecki; editing by David Gaffen)

Source: Reuters

items.title: AI data center stocks dip, renewables surge after Democrat sweep in US midterm elections
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: AI data centre stocks declined while renewable energy and healthcare shares rallied after Democrats won control of Congress in the US midterm elections. Investors assessed the possibility of tighter AI oversight and continued clean energy support. Defence contractors and prison operators fell amid concerns over changing government spending and immigration policies.
items.body: Data center stocks slid on Wednesday, while clean-energy shares rallied after Democrats seized control of Congress, prompting investors to reposition for tougher scrutiny of the AI boom and a shift in policy priorities.The Democratic sweep, which included victories in traditional Republican strongholds and key data-center hubs Texas and Georgia, will usher in divided government in Washington and raises the prospect of greater congressional oversight of industries that benefited from Republican control.Market reaction rippled across AI-linked stocks, renewables, healthcare companies, defense contractors and prison operators.DATA CENTER STOCKSData center operators lost ground, with Core Scientific down 3.5% and Iren down 3.6%. Applied Digital and CoreWeave fell 2.4% and 3.8%, respectively.The data center boom sparked public backlash this year, raising concerns that tighter Democratic oversight could slow investment just as investors grow wary of soaring AI spending and uncertain returns.Though analysts doubt any legislation could meaningfully stall data center construction, a Democratic-led Congress increases prospects of more hearings and investigations related to the AI buildout. AI has been an enormous engine powering the US economy, so any curbs on its future development could threaten to put the brakes on growth, said Kit Rees, investment strategist at Quilter.CLEAN ENERGYA Democratic sweep could bolster expectations for continued federal support for clean energy while speeding approvals for energy and infrastructure projects.Democrats plan to scrutinize the Trump administration's efforts to roll back emissions rules and could use the Congressional Review Act to overturn regulations that make it easier to sell gas-powered trucks and SUVs.Shares of solar maker First Solar gained 7%, residential solar installer Sunrun added 6.1% and inverter maker Enphase Energy was up 3.6%. Clean-power developer NextEra Energy inched 2.3% higher. The more that oil and gas prices rise, the bigger the incentive, the bigger the economic incentive to roll out clean energy, said Paul Jackson, global market strategist for EMEA at Invesco.Europe's Vestas and Orsted rose 4.3% and 6.4%, respectively, while Portugal's EDP Renewables was up 2.3%.ELON MUSK-LED COMPANIESShares of Elon Musk's rocket and space technology company SpaceX dropped 5.2%, while EV maker Tesla was down 4.9%. It puts into doubt a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla. While Congress cannot stop a merger, they could slow it down via extra scrutiny, said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB. Musk had poured hundreds of millions into the Republican Party ahead of these elections...we could see stocks linked to Musk struggle now that his political enemies have won back control of Congress. Trump Media & Technology Group, majority-owned by Trump, dropped 7.7%.DEFENSE STOCKSDefense contractors such as Northrop Grumman fell 2.7%, while RTX, Lockheed Martin and L3Harris lost over 2% each. The sector had been underpinned by expectations that the $1.5-trillion budget request by Trump would not face headwinds in a Republican-dominated Congress.However, in a Democrat-led Congress, analysts project the funding could fall short of expectations.HEALTH INSURERS AND HOSPITAL OPERATORSShares of hospital operators such as HCA Healthcare and Universal Health Services gained 5.4% and 3.4%, respectively.Insurers such as Centene rose 4.7% and Elevance was marginally higher.Democrats have pushed for universal healthcare policies that could mean more government spending allocated to the sector.BNP Paribas economist Anis Bensaidani said Democrats may lack the numbers to pass legislation restoring major parts of the Affordable Care Act, but they could still win concessions while negotiating over defense spending and government funding.PRISON OPERATORSPrison operators such as GEO Group and CoreCivic fell 6.2% and 5.7%, respectively. The two stocks have rallied sharply since Trump won the presidency two years ago, as his clampdown on illegal immigration boosted the need for detention facilities.

[４日　ロイター] - 米ファストフードチェーン大手マクドナルドが４日発表した２０２６年第３・四半期（２６年７─９月期）決算は、主要市場の米国で既存店売上高が前年同期比０．２％減と、６四半期ぶりの減少となった。生活費の高騰で消費者が外食を控える傾向が続いたことが響いた。より安価なメニューを持つ同業との競争も激化している。

ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリスト予想は０．１％減だった。

世界全体の既存店売上高は１．５％増で、市場予想と同程度だった。調整後１株当たり利益は３．５７ドル。前年同期の３．２２ドルから増加し、予想の３．３８ドルを上回った。営業コスト・経費が約４％減少したことが寄与した。

マクドナルドは３ドル以下のメニューや４ドルの朝食セットなど低所得層向けに「バリューメニュー」を展開してきたが、情報分析会社Ｐｌａｃｅｒ．ａｉのデータによると、来店客数は４．６％減だったという。

マクドナルドのクリス・ケンプチンスキ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、価格面での取り組みを進め、足元では改善が見られていると明らかにした。イアン・ボーデン最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は９月下旬の投資家向けイベントで、９月単月の売上高はプラスに復調するとの見通しを示していた。

２０２５年８月撮影　REUTERS/Dado Ruvic（ロイター） Neil J Kanatt　Waylon Cunningham

[４日　ロイター] - 米ファストフードチェーン大手マクドナルドが４日発表した２０２６年第３・四半期（２６年７─９月期）決算は、主要市場の米国で既存店売上高が前年同期比０．２％減と、６四半期ぶりの減少となった。生活費の高騰で消費者が外食を控える傾向が続いたことが響いた。より安価なメニューを持つ同業との競争も激化している。

ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリスト予想は０．１％減だった。

世界全体の既存店売上高は１．５％増で、市場予想と同程度だった。調整後１株当たり利益は３．５７ドル。前年同期の３．２２ドルから増加し、予想の３．３８ドルを上回った。営業コスト・経費が約４％減少したことが寄与した。

マクドナルドは３ドル以下のメニューや４ドルの朝食セットなど低所得層向けに「バリューメニュー」を展開してきたが、情報分析会社Ｐｌａｃｅｒ．ａｉのデータによると、来店客数は４．６％減だったという。

マクドナルドのクリス・ケンプチンスキ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、価格面での取り組みを進め、足元では改善が見られていると明らかにした。イアン・ボーデン最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は９月下旬の投資家向けイベントで、９月単月の売上高はプラスに復調するとの見通しを示していた。

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 4 : The dollar retreated on Wednesday but was off its earlier lows after a sweeping victory by Democrats in the US midterm elections removed a source of uncertainty for the market while investors gauged the potential for regulatory changes.
Democrats seized control of both the Senate and House of Representatives on Tuesday, scoring sweeping victories in some Republican strongholds for the first time in generations as tens of millions of voters delivered a sharp rebuke to President Donald Trump.
The outsized win eased concerns about potentially contested results, although it brought the prospect of divided government and legislative gridlock between a Republican White House and a Democratic Congress, as the US grapples with the Iran war and an AI boom that has fuelled both economic growth and inflation.
US stocks rallied, with the S&P 500 up about 2 per cent, while crude prices plummeted as investors waited for Washington's next move in the US-Israeli war with Iran.

"It's a risk-on feeling. Maybe we're just seeing a bit of a combination of sell the news, buy the fact, relief that we're not going to be in a quagmire over rigged election results," said Erik Bregar, director of FX and precious metals risk management at Silver Gold Bull in Toronto.
"Fundamentally, you could still see more of the AI concerns, given the Democrat positioning on data centers and all. But for the time being, markets are relieved that Trump's not going to fight this, and when we see risk-on across the board, that's broadly dollar negative."
DOLLAR INDEX FALLS, EURO CLIMBS
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, fell 0.25 per cent to 101.60 after earlier falling to 101.21, its lowest since September 30. The euro was up 0.21 per cent at $1.1217 after climbing to $1.1272, its highest since October 6.
Despite the political shift in the US, expectations for the Federal Reserve's interest rate path remained largely intact. Markets are pricing in an 81.2 per cent chance for a rate increase of at least 25 basis points from the Fed at its December meeting, according to CME FedWatch, up from 77.4 per cent in the prior session.
PAYROLLS BEAT EXPECTATIONS
The election results largely overshadowed a flurry of US economic data.
The ADP National Employment Report showed US private payrolls rose by 86,000 jobs in October, above the 69,000 estimate of economists polled by Reuters. The report was the latest in a string of labor market data this week, which will wind up on Friday with the release of the government's payrolls report.
A separate report from the Institute for Supply Management said its non-manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index dipped to 54.5 last month, down from 54.9 in September. The latest reading was slightly below economists' 54.8 estimate but above the 50 threshold that signifies expansion.
Sterling was up 0.38 per cent at $1.3462, after rising to a more than seven-week high of $1.3503 ahead of the Bank of England's policy announcement on Thursday. The pound was poised for its sixth straight daily gain, its longest run higher since an eight-session streak that ended on July 6.
The Bank of England is expected to bow to inflation pressure from soaring energy costs and raise interest rates, although it may push back against investors' bets that several more increases will follow next year.
Against the Japanese yen, the dollar weakened 0.14 per cent to 158.43.

items.title: 米共和党ジョンソン下院議長、少数党院内総務選に不出馬＝関係筋
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
David Morgan

[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
David Morgan

[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - 米共和党のジョンソン下院議長は、３日投開票の中間選挙で共和党が下院の多数派を失ったことを受け、下院共和党トップの少数党院内総務選に立候補しない意向を固めた。関係筋が４日、明らかにした。

関係筋によると、ジョンソン氏は４日朝、スタッフに決定を伝えた。ジョンソン氏は３年前に下院議長に就任して以降、２１８対２１４の僅差だった共和党多数派の取りまとめに苦慮していた。

トランプ大統領は記者団に対し、共和党の指導部選には関与しないとの考えを示した上で、「（ジョンソン）議長はすばらしかった。彼の部下たちもすばらしかった。みんな良い人たちだ」と語った。 

こうした中、１０日に実施される見通しの党内選挙で、オハイオ州選出の保守強硬派ジム・ジョーダン議員とスカリス下院院内総務は、少数党院内総務ポストを目指す方針を表明した。

ジョーダン氏は同僚議員への書簡で立候補を表明。法と秩序、減税、伝統的価値観を優先課題として挙げ、「われわれが多数派を取り戻すには、これらの原則を実行する能力に対する有権者の信頼を回復しなければならない」と述べた。

スカリス氏も同僚議員への書簡で、「真の米国」に暮らす人々と対話し、その意見を基に社会保障や高齢者向け公的医療保険（メディケア）など主要課題に関する法案を策定するための作業部会を設置すると提案。「われわれには大きな課題が待ち受けており、実績のあるリーダーシップが今ほど必要とされている時はない」と述べた。

ジョーダン氏とスカリス氏は、２０２３年に共和党強硬派がマッカーシー氏を下院議長の座から追放した後、それぞれ議長選に立候補したが、いずれも失敗に終わった。

items.title: 世界企業、コストや関税巡る短期見通し変わらず　民主が米議会掌握でも
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Christoph Steitz　Yuka Obayashi　Emanuele Berro

[フランクフルト／東京／グダニスク ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Christoph Steitz　Yuka Obayashi　Emanuele Berro

[フランクフルト／東京／グダニスク ４日 ロイター] - 世界の企業各社は４日、エネルギーや原材料のコスト上昇、米消費者の購買力の低下に苦しむ中、米連邦議会の民主党による掌握が短期的な見通しを変える可能性は低いとの見方を示した。一方で、政治的安定が見込まれることを歓迎する声もあった。 

３日投開票の米中間選挙では、民主党が上下両院の過半数を奪還した。共和党の牙城にも食い込んで幅広い勝利を収め、有権者がトランプ大統領に厳しい審判を下した形となった。

だが、関税措置やエネルギー価格、インフレ、消費者信頼感など、世界中の企業を揺るがしている問題に対して、今回の結果が何を意味するのかを見極めるには時期尚早だ。 

ドイツの自動車部品大手コンチネンタルのローランド・ウェルツバッハー最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は「米国で事業を展開する企業としてわれわれに必要なのは、政治的安定と信頼できる経済の枠組みだ。これらを支えるあらゆる動きは歓迎する」と指摘。「これが当社や経済全体にとって具体的に何を意味するのかはまだ不明だが、安定をもたらすという点では良いことだ」と述べた。

アナリストらは、米国の消費者のコストを押し上げてきた貿易戦争への回帰を避けるため、ホワイトハウスへの圧力が強まる可能性があると指摘。一方、欧州の一部メーカーは、トランプ氏の高い輸入関税が即座に実質的に緩和されることはほとんど期待できないとみている。  

ドイツ機械工業連盟（ＶＤＭＡ）で北米担当の通商政策顧問を務めるアンドリュー・アデア氏は、トランプ政権は主に議会の承認を必要としない大統領権限を通じて関税政策を進めてきたため、こうした権限は依然として維持されるとの見方を示した。

同氏は、議会は既存の関税の撤回を模索する可能性はあるものの、そうした法案は大きな政治的ハードルに直面し、最終的に大統領に拒否権を行使される可能性があると指摘。「このため、国内政治が短期的に事業環境に直接影響を及ぼすとは予想していない」と語った。

今回の選挙結果は、トランプ氏の強硬な移民・通商政策によって損なわれてきた米国の対外的なイメージを改善させる可能性もある。トランプ氏の就任以降、訪米者数は大きく落ち込んでいる。

独フランクフルト空港運営会社フラポートのステファン・シュルテＣＥＯは「関税を巡る反発が和らぎ、旅行への意欲が高まる可能性があり、航空業界にかなりプラスの影響を与えるはずだ」としつつ、「ただ、その重要性を過大評価するつもりはない」と述べた。

Nov 4 : An AI chip boom is redirecting semiconductor supply toward data centres and away from smartphones and PCs, constraining some end markets, Siltronic CEO Michael Heckmeier said on Wednesday.
Siltronic, which makes silicon wafers used in semiconductors, raised its annual sales forecast for the second time this year on Wednesday, citing stronger demand for its wafers.
AI-linked demand has become the chip industry's main growth engine, but Heckmeier told Reuters in an interview that some other semiconductor end markets could grow faster if more chips were available.
"It's not that AI is offsetting certain weaknesses," Heckmeier said. "It's more AI is generating a certain weakness."

Demand for AI-related chips remains so strong that semiconductor manufacturers are allocating more supply to those applications, leaving less capacity for other end markets.
"When our customers have the choice to sell their chips to different segments, they will always send them to the ones that pay best," he said. "The pockets of the AI players, particularly the hyperscalers, are the deepest."
The trend has made AI servers the industry's main growth engine, with the impact extending beyond higher server volumes.
Heckmeier said AI server farms consume roughly three to four times more silicon area than traditional servers, boosting demand for advanced wafers
Any moderation in AI demand would not necessarily derail the industry's growth, Heckmeier said, because capacity could flow back to smartphones, PCs and other markets where underlying demand remains solid.
"We don't see it at all today," Heckmeier said of any slowdown in AI demand.
"But even if it came, we feel there is a natural balance in the system that the overall growth dynamics could go on."

[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Howard Schneider

[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - 中間選挙での民主党の圧勝、とりわけ米上院の支配権獲得は、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）への介入を図るトランプ大統領に対し、ＦＲＢの立場を強める結果となる。上院が人事承認権を握ることは、トランプ氏が中央銀行にこれ以上の盟友を送り込むことへの大きな歯止めとなる。

これは、ウォーシュ議長にとっても新たな頭痛の種になりかねない。主要な監督委員会が民主党の手に渡り、上院銀行委員会の場合、ウォーシュ氏に厳しい批判を向けてきたマサチューセッツ州選出のエリザベス・ウォーレン上院議員（民主党）が、トランプ氏の盟友でウォーシュ氏を支持するサウスカロライナ州選出のティム・スコット氏に代わって委員長に就く可能性が高いためだ。

元ＦＲＢ理事ラリー・メイヤー氏の会社であるマネタリー・ポリシー・アナリティクスのエコノミストらは、民主党の上院勝利の影響について、ウォーシュ氏は「議長就任で民主党からの支持を得られなかった。発信を減らし、対外的な透明性が低下した中銀運営を進める中で、敵対的な質問がウォーシュ氏の姿勢を試すことになりかねない」と記した。

生活費問題を前面に掲げて選挙戦を展開した民主党には、中央銀行のインフレ抑制という使命を巡ってウォーシュ氏に圧力をかける動機がある。一方、同委員会は重要と見なす問題を調査する広い余地を持つことになる。ウォーレン氏の場合、ウォーシュ氏がＦＲＢ議長に就任する過程で数億ドルの資産を不透明な形で処理したことなどがそれに当たる。

トランプ氏にとって、議会の新たな力学は、７人で構成するＦＲＢ理事会にさらに盟友を据えようとする取り組みを直接阻むものだ。理事のうち３人はバイデン前大統領が任命した。トランプ氏とバイデン氏から連続して任命されながら、今は大統領と対立するパウエル前議長も、依然として理事にとどまっている。

大統領はこの顔ぶれを「敵対的」「党派的」と呼び、ＦＲＢは金利を大幅に引き下げる必要があると主張してきた。反対に、ウォーシュ氏を含む政策当局者は、高インフレを抑えるために利上げを続けてきた。

トランプ氏によるリサ・クック理事の解任の試みは続いている。数週間以内にホワイトハウスの行政手続きが行われる見通しで、クック氏がＦＲＢに任命される前の住宅ローン申請の誤りを巡り、トランプ氏が解任する「正当な理由」があると表明する下地を整えるものとみられる。

これに対しては訴訟が起こされる公算が大きい。最高裁は既に一度、クック氏の排除を図る試みに対しトランプ氏に不利な判断を下している。仮に最終的に解任に成功したとしても、民主党主導の上院が後任候補を承認する見込みはほとんどない。

共和党が支配する機関でさえ、トランプ氏の１期目には極端と見なされたＦＲＢ人事を拒否した。今年は、ノースカロライナ州選出のトム・ティリス上院議員（共和党）が、政権がパウエル氏に対する刑事捜査を取り下げるまでウォーシュ氏の指名を保留した経緯がある。トランプ氏から圧力を受けた後、ティリス氏は再選出馬を見送り、同州は民主党のロイ・クーパー氏が制した。

ＦＲＢ政治を扱った著書を持つパイロット・ウェーブ・ホールディングスのパートナー、マーク・スピンデル氏は、今回の選挙の影響に関する分析で、民主党が支配する上院は「今後のトランプ氏の指名候補を巡る承認環境を変え、ＦＲＢに異なる程度の政治的支援を与える可能性がある」と記した。ＦＲＢの独立性は「常に部分的に議会に依存してきた。上院からの制度的な支援は、政策当局者が政治的圧力ではなくインフレや雇用に基づいて決定を下す余地がどれだけあるかに影響を与え得る」と指摘した。

上院の委員会に加え、下院金融サービス委員会も民主党が支配することで、政権や現職のミシェル・ボウマン監督担当副議長が推し進める銀行・規制改革を巡る混乱も招きかねない。ＦＲＢはステーブルコインを規制する「ジーニアス法」などに関する規則を策定中で、ボウマン氏は最近、ＦＲＢの銀行監督体制の統合を打ち出した。

World stocks rally as investors expect more political certainty after Democrats' win

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 4 : Global stocks rallied on Wednesday after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections, providing greater political clarity and reducing the uncertainty that has weighed on markets. 
Brent crude oil futures were down 9 per cent at $94.50 a barrel as investors weighed Washington's next move in talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against worries that recent attacks in both conflicts could further disrupt supplies.
In a major setback to President Donald Trump, Democrats scored sweeping victories in Republican strongholds for the first time in generations. The breadth of the party's success was underscored by gains in districts long considered safely conservative, highlighting a political shift that may have caught some investors off guard.
On Wall Street, all three main indexes were trading higher with communication services, consumer discretionary and consumer staples stocks driving gains. Energy shares were the biggest losers on the day with crude prices down as Trump acknowledged that the Iran war had played a role in his party's sweeping defeat.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 2.89 per cent, the S&P 500 was up 1.85 per cent, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 2.13 per cent.
"Markets hate uncertainty and even though a lot of what the result was had been priced in ahead of time, getting confirmation of that last night brings certainty to markets," said Clayton Allison, portfolio manager at Prime Capital Financial. "Now this brings questions as to what actually gets done in Washington over the next two years. But the markets love to see that there is a resolution to a catalyst event."
Opinion polls have shown Democratic voters favouring more control over AI, and investors expect the Democratic-controlled Congress to apply more scrutiny to the sector.
The MSCI All-World index was up 1.56 per cent, while Europe's STOXX 600, which has acted as a hedge against AI-related risks, jumped 1.87 per cent to two-month highs. 
AI stocks in Asia initially led a decline in equity markets before finishing higher overnight. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.41 per cent.
The AI boom has helped propel global markets in recent years, driven by heavy spending from tech giants racing to build data centers and expand computing capacity. That has made investors acutely sensitive to anything that could derail the technology's rapid expansion.
Advanced Micro Devices rose nearly 1 per cent after the US chipmaker forecast faster growth through 2027, reassuring investors that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong.
SAFE-HAVEN BID
Treasuries rallied as investors expect gridlock in Washington to cut government spending, with AI regulation also possibly slowing growth and reducing the need for rate hikes.
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was down 5.18 basis points on the day at 4.90 per cent, having fallen as much as 6 bps to a low of 4.89 per cent overnight, which, in turn, weighed on the dollar. 
The broadly weaker dollar left the euro up 0.38 per cent at $1.1235 and the pound up 0.45 per cent at $1.3472.
The yen and the Swiss franc — both safe-haven currencies — also notched gains. The Swiss franc was up 0.50 per cent against the dollar at 0.817 francs. The Japanese yen rose 0.27 per cent to 158.24.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin gained 3.22 per cent to $80,316.07. Ethereum rose 5.8 per cent to $2,425.26.
Spot gold rose 3.57 per cent to $4,068.62 an ounce.

Source: Reuters

items.title: カルシなどの予測市場、米中間選挙結果ほぼ的中　一部波乱も
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - ３日投開票の米中間選挙では、野党・民主党が連邦議会の上下両院で多数派を奪還したが、一部の選挙区で予想外の結果も見られたものの、カルシやポリマーケットなどの予測市場で全体的な結果がおおむね正確に見通されていたことが分かった。

今回の中間選挙では１４億８０００万ドル超が賭けられ、予測市場で示された勝敗確率が実際の選挙結果をどの程度正確に予測できるかを測る試金石になっていた。

接戦が予想された複数の上院選では数百万ドル規模の賭けが集まった。多くのケースで結果は市場予想に沿う形となり、民主党はテキサス州やオハイオ州で上院議席を獲得。一部では勝敗予想が外れた選挙区もあったが、数千万人の有権者がトランプ大統領に厳しい審判を下す中、民主党の上下両院制覇に賭けた参加者の多くは利益を得た。

デジタル資産取引プラットフォーム、タロスの調査責任者ケリー・イェ氏は「予測市場は数時間以内に中間選挙の結果を織り込んだ」と指摘。米ラトガース大学のハリー・クレーン教授（統計学）は「今回が真の意味で初めての予測市場選挙だった」とし、「市場は選挙戦終盤の数週間を通じて民主党優勢を予想し続け、投票結果が判明するにつれてリアルタイムで素早く反応した」と語った。

予測市場運営会社カルシの選挙関連市場の取引額は今回、２５億ドルを超えた。大統領選を含んだ２０２４年の選挙サイクルでは１３億ドルだった。

カルシの参加者は４月時点で、民主党が大勝する「ブルー・ツナミ」の確率を５５％と見積もっていた。一方、事情に詳しい関係者によると、ポリマーケットの選挙予測は約９８％の精度だった。

一方、市場予想が大きく外れた例としては、保守地盤のサウスカロライナ州の上院選が挙げられる。カルシとポリマーケットは３日午後時点で、故リンゼー・グラハム元上院議員の妹である共和党候補ダーリーン・グラハム氏が勝利する確率を７０％と見積もっていた。しかし、民主党候補のアニー・アンドルーズ氏が勝利した。

米資産運用会社アネックス・ウェルス・マネジメントのブライアン・ジェイコブセン主席エコノミストは「予測市場は、単に意見を表明するのではなく、正しい予測をする動機を持った人々の見方を集約するため有用だ」と指摘。「情報全体がどの方向を示しているかを知る手掛かりにはなるが、予測は約束ではない。政治であれスポーツであれ、結果を知るには実際に選挙を行い、試合をしてみる必要がある」と述べた。

予測市場は２０２４年の米大統領選でトランプ氏勝利の可能性を示し、従来の世論調査と異なる見通しを示したことで注目を集めた。アナリストらは今週、その予測精度を注視していた。

市場運営会社は高い予測精度をうたう一方、米予備選やブラジル大統領選では予測外れの例もあり、完全ではないことも示されている。予測市場では、利用者が現実の出来事に連動する契約を売買し、その価格が参加者全体の予想を反映。ただ、投機的取引や流動性不足、大口投資家による集中した賭けによって確率が歪められる可能性があるとの指摘も出ている。

Chinese genetic firm Novogene sues US over military designation

FILE PHOTO: The Pentagon building, pictured from the Washington Monument in Washington, D.C., U.S., June 24, 2026. REUTERS/Tom Brenner/File photo

WASHINGTON, Nov 4 : Chinese genetic sequencing firm Novogene sued the Pentagon late Tuesday in US District Court in Washington over its inclusion on a US list of companies allegedly aiding Beijing's military.
In June, the Defense Department added Novogene, Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba, internet search provider Baidu and automakers BYD and NIO and others to its list of "Chinese military companies" that prohibits the Defense Department from contracting directly with the firms.
Novogene noted its US unit employs about 180 people at its Sacramento office and at sequencing centers in Sacramento,
California, and Beaverton, Oregon. "Novogene does not design, develop, or market products for military use," the company's lawsuit said. The company called the designation unlawful and said it has resulted in "serious, irreparable, and unwarranted economic, reputational, and other harm."

The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The designation does not impose formal sanctions but starting in 2027 restricts purchases of their products or services by the Pentagon through third parties.
A number of Chinese firms have sued the Pentagon over the designations. Last week, a US judge granted Alibaba Group Holding's request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the US government not to deny Pentagon contracts after the company sued over its designation.
Last month, two subsidiaries of BYD sued the Pentagon over a federal law banning any Pentagon contractors from hiring lobbyists that also work with blacklisted firms, arguing that it breached BYD's First Amendment rights.
In August, DJI, the world's largest drone maker, appealed its inclusion on the blacklist with the court finding merit in its argument that unclassified records did not support the conclusion that the company contributed to the Chinese defense industrial base.
The appeals court ordered the lower court to reconsider its decision to reject DJI's bid to be removed from the Pentagon list and the case is ongoing. In August, biotech firm WuXi AppTec Co also won a preliminary injunction from a US federal court, which blocked its inclusion on the list. WuXi said the Pentagon designation was politically motivated.

Source: Reuters

items.title: アングル：米中間選挙の民主勝利、市場に新たな波乱　外交・財政リスク警戒
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Dhara Ranasinghe　Ankur Banerjee

[ロンドン ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Dhara Ranasinghe　Ankur Banerjee

[ロンドン ４日 ロイター] - 米中間選挙での民主党の圧勝は、市場にとって新たな波乱要因となった。市場は既に、イラン戦争の余波に加え、成長とインフレを押し上げてきたＡＩ（人工知能）ブーム、そして米国の債務拡大への対応に追われている。

投資家は市場の変動が続くとみて身構えている。特に２つの分野に注目が集まっている。今年に入り原油価格を７０％押し上げてきたイラン戦争の行方と、米国の財政支出を巡る激しい論争だ。

約６０００億ドルの資産を運用するＲＢＣブルーベイ・アセット・マネジメントのマーケット戦略責任者マイク・ベル氏は「市場にとって最大の潜在的な影響は、中間選挙という障害がなくなった今、トランプ大統領が中東でのエスカレーションに踏み切ると決断した場合だろう。エスカレーションが続きエネルギー価格が上昇すれば、株式と債券が同時に打撃を受ける可能性がある」と語った。

イラン戦争が続く中、原油価格は１バレル＝１００ドルを超える水準で高止まりし、消費者や企業の燃料コストを押し上げている。一方、中央銀行は、より大幅な利上げを迫られるような広範な物価急騰への波及リスクに警戒を強めている。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は、５年以上にわたってインフレ目標を達成できていない。ユーロ圏でも、１０月のインフレ率はエネルギー高を背景に４％と３年ぶりの高水準に上昇した。今後数カ月でさらに上がる見通しだ。これにより、１２月の欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の利上げを巡る市場の観測が改めて裏付けられた。

アナリストによると、トランプ氏が外交政策の主導権を握り続けるため、地政学的リスクは引き続き高いという。

イラン戦争に加え、今年は、米国によるベネズエラのマドゥロ大統領の拘束や、デンマーク自治領グリーンランドを巡ってトランプ氏が欧州の同盟国に関税で脅しをかけたことも、投資家の不意を突いた。

ベレンベルクのチーフエコノミスト、ホルガー・シュミーディング氏は「トランプ政権の残り２年間は、外交政策を巡る大きな混乱に備えなければならないだろう」と述べた。

＜ＡＩ投資から債務へ＞

民主党の勝利を受けて規制面での監視強化がＡＩ分野の急成長を妨げかねないとの懸念が、市場の当面の焦点となった。

世論調査では、民主党支持者がＡＩへの規制強化を支持していることが示されており、投資家は民主党が多数派を占める議会が同分野への監視を強めると予想している。

プリンシパル・アセット・マネジメントのチーフグローバルストラテジスト、シーマ・シャー氏は「ＡＩは米国の成長ストーリーの極めて重要な部分を占めている。だから、どの政党が政権を握ろうとも、投資の拡大を支えつつコスト面の懸念に配慮するという、両方のいいとこ取りを目指すだろう」と述べた。同氏は、第２次世界大戦終結以降、Ｓ＆Ｐ株価指数が中間選挙の１年後にはいずれの場合も上昇していると指摘した。

それでも投資家は、市場の底堅さについて神経質になってきている。ＡＩの設備投資急増と多額の債務を抱える政府が、金利を数十年ぶりの高水準に押し上げ、市場の弱点を露呈させてきた。

シャー氏は、選挙結果を受けて一段と制約を受ける可能性がある財政政策の行方を注視すると付け加えた。

アナリストからは、共和党が勝利した場合に米成人に５０００ドルの小切手を配るというトランプ氏の公約が実現しないことへの安堵が示された。

ソシエテ・ジェネラルの新興国リサーチ世界責任者フェニックス・カレン氏は、民主党が議会を支配すれば、財政政策への監視が強まり、トランプ氏が支出拡大の面でできることに歯止めがかかる公算が大きいと指摘。「それは財政政策により厳しい制約を課すものであり、米国債利回りへの圧力を幾分和らげる助けになるはずだ」と語った。

４０兆ドルを超える米国の債務残高への懸念は、今年の国債利回りを押し上げる一因となってきた。

議会は２０２７会計年度の支出を巡る激しい論争を中間選挙後に先送りしており、資金調達合意に達するための期限を１２月１１日に設定した。

債務上限引き上げの期限は２０２７年後半まで到来しない見通しだが、民主党はいわゆる「Ｘデート」を、支出・税制政策を巡る共和党との交渉の切り札として使える可能性がある。借り入れ上限への対応に向けた賛成票と引き換えに、譲歩を迫るものだ。

シャー氏は「市場の変動は続くとみている。今後１年は手に汗握る展開になるだろう」と述べた。

items.title: Iranian officials gloat as US voters deal blow to Trump
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that US hostility would persist regardless of which party was in power.

Iranian officials gloat as US voters deal blow to Trump

Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that US hostility would persist regardless of which party was in power.

Women gather next to an anti-US mural, showing the Statue of Liberty with a severed arm, during the 47th anniversary of the US expulsion from Iran, in Tehran, Nov 4, 2026. (Photo: West Asia News Agency via REUTERS/ Majid Asgaripour)

IRAN: Iran's government savoured the stinging rebuke delivered to Donald Trump in the midterm elections, declaring voters had rejected the war launched by the US president even as Tehran remained on high alert for the possibility of renewed strikes.
"Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, Iran's chief negotiator, posted on X on Wednesday (Nov 4), adding that Washington should not ignore public opinion by attacking his country again.
Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that US hostility would persist regardless of which party was in power, warning against "even the slightest inclination towards submission" to the US .
"The US sees the end of its hegemony as distant; we see it as near," he added.

Democrats captured majorities in both the Senate and Ho us e in Tuesday's election , with victories in Republican strongholds underscoring deep fr us tration with Trump 's stewardship of the economy and his decision to launch a war that drove up gas prices.
In Iran, a news outlet run by the judiciary shared a joke circulating on X that " Trump failed at regime change in Iran but he succeeded in Texas", a reference to the southern state where a Democrat won a Senate race for the first time in decades.
But two senior Iranian sources told Reuters that while Iranian leaders welcomed the Democrats’ victory, Tehran was concerned that Trump could seek to compensate for it with a military strike, and remained on high alert.
Iran's leaders have long regarded the United States as their main enemy, referring to it as "the Great Satan".
At a state-organised rally on Wednesday commemorating the student takeover of the US embassy in Tehran during the 1979 Islamic revolution, demonstrators voiced triumph at an election they linked to Iran's success in surviving months of US attacks.
"The fact that the might of these warmongering Republicans has been broken, something unprecedented in human history, means that from now on we will see the real war unfolding inside the US Senate and among American officials ," said one, giving only his family name of Nazari.

Pictures of US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, on a dartboard during the 47th anniversary of the US expulsion from Iran, in Tehran, Nov 4, 2026. (Photo: West Asia News Agency via REUTERS/Majid Asgaripour)

Mediators have intensified efforts to end the war amid fears it could reignite after the election , with Trump on Tuesday declining to rule out a resumption of combat operations after the vote and Iran planning wider retaliation if war resumes.
The US and Israel attacked Iran on Feb 28, and Iran responded with strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. Conflict also erupted in Lebanon between Iran-backed Hezbollah and Israel, and more recently spread to Yemen, from where the Iran-aligned Houthis have struck energy facilities, airports and other targets in Saudi Arabia.
Global oil and gas prices have shot up with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz severely disrupted after Tehran declared it closed, while the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iran, hitting Iran's economy hard.
"IRAN'S SHADOW OVER US ELECTIONS" Ahead of the US election, senior Iranian officials told Reuters that Tehran was deliberately prolonging talks with the US to weaken Trump politically ahead of the vote.
Some news outlets played on the timing of the election on the anniversary of the embassy seizure, when radical students cemented Iran's toppling of the US -backed Shah by storming the embassy and holding 52 Americans hostage there for 444 days.
Major Iranian newspaper Hamshahri linked the events with a front-page image showing Trump blindfolded with his head bowed.
With a headline declaring "Iran's shadow over US elections", it said Washington had been "47 years Iran's captive: from the capture of the spies' nest ( US embassy) to the November 2026 US Congress elections".
The Iran war has been unpopular among Americans since it began, and blaming the war for driving up costs was a foc us of the Democrats' election campaign.
Khamenei's message signalled that Tehran had no intention of showing flexibility on its demands for lasting control over the Strait of Hormuz or conditions to end the conflict.
"The consequences of ( US ) miscalculations and arrogant del us ions have manifested as a heavy burden of costs, borne by the American people and the puppet regimes subservient to the US government," he said.
Trump has offered shifting goals and timelines for the war that is now in its ninth month.
"I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran," Trump told Fox News, referring to the election result.
The conservative Iranian newspaper Jam-e Jam declared the election result "The twilight of Trump ism".

Why Europe's supermarket fridges were easy targets

FAST

BRUGES, Belgium, Nov 4 : Hackers who cranked up fridge temperatures at supermarkets across Europe may have gained access through public internet-connected systems protected by default passwords or outdated software, a cybersecurity expert said.
The second cyberattack in three weeks hit fridge systems at supermarket chains including Carrefour and Delhaize in Belgium, and ICA and Coop in Sweden, forcing retailers to discard spoiled food and raising concerns about food security. Three blood banks in France were also hit.
Authorities have not publicly disclosed how the attackers gained access, and no perpetrator has been identified.
Laurens Singier, an ethical hacker and researcher at Cyber 3 Lab, part of Howest University of Applied Sciences in Bruges, Belgium, said internet-connected systems which can be accessible remotely often have weak protections.

"In this case, the weak point was mainly putting those devices on the public internet. They shouldn't even be there," he said, speaking from a lab full of servers and systems similar to those that could control supermarket store fridges.
A common problem with such systems is that operators fail to change default passwords set by the manufacturer, while others run older software with known vulnerabilities, he said.
AI was now making it easier for amateurs to pull off hacks, Singier added.
Supermarkets on Tuesday said they had taken hacked fridges offline, in line with guidance from refrigeration monitoring software provider Danfoss, whose systems were again among those targeted. Danfoss has said it is working with clients on fixes.
Singier said that retailers should check they understand how they connect to the store interface, strengthen passwords, and consider switching from internet-based systems to more secure systems using SIM cards, like those used by solar panels and car chargers.
"After this attack, we've seen a lot less of these devices publicly on the internet," he said. "But if you look at the numbers, there's still a lot of industrial devices which are open to the public, and in a lot of cases you yourself as the butcher or the chocolatier don't even know about it."

PARIS, Nov 4 : Online fashion retailer Shein said on Wednesday it would invest €500 million ($562 million) to expand its European logistics hub in Poland as it pursues faster deliveries and greater operational flexibility.
Shein, along with Chinese competitors such as Temu and AliExpress, is adapting to charges imposed in July to curb what the EU says is unfair competition from online retailers. 
• The EU initially introduced a €3 fee for parcels worth less than €150, and increased the levy by €2 on November 1
• Shein's sales in Europe dropped sharply in the second quarter, contributing to a 67 per cent net profit fall

[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - 米供給管理協会（ＩＳＭ）が４日発表した１０月の非製造業購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）は５４．５と、前月の５４．９から小幅に低下した。新規事業の勢いが鈍化した。一方、供給網の混乱は続き、投入価格は高止まりした。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は５４．８だった。

ＰＭＩは第４・四半期の米経済が堅調な滑り出しとなったことを示した。ただ、エコノミストは景気の減速を予想している。個人消費は２四半期続けて力強く伸びたが、今後は減速するとみられている。高インフレが家計の購買力を圧迫しており、消費を抑える一因になるとみられる。

１０月の新規事業指数は５５．９と、９月の５９．８から低下した。イラン戦争や輸入関税の影響で、供給業者の納入状況は一段と悪化した。

供給業者の納入状況を示す指数は５６．７と、９月の５３．２から大幅に上昇した。５０を上回ると納入の遅れを示す。納入の遅れは２３カ月連続となり、投入価格の高止まりにつながっている。

投入コストを示す支払価格指数は７３．０と、９月の７４．０から低下したものの、なお高水準だった。

雇用指数は５０．１から５１．４へ上昇した。

items.title: ネタニヤフ氏の政敵ら、首相抜きの政権樹立狙う　米議会での民主勝利受け
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Steven Scheer　Alexander Cornwell

[エルサレム ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Steven Scheer　Alexander Cornwell

[エルサレム ４日 ロイター] - イスラエルのネタニヤフ首相の政敵らは、米民主党が議会を制したことは、同氏が米国による何世代にもわたるイスラエルに対する超党派的な支持を台無しにした証拠だとし、同氏抜きでの政権を樹立する機会をうかがっている。

３日投開票の米中間選挙では、民主党が上下両院の過半数を奪還した。不人気な対イラン戦争への強い不満や生活費高騰への不安、トランプ大統領の政権運営に対する怒りが背景にある。

米国は何世代にもわたり、両党の歴代大統領の下でイスラエルの最も強固な同盟国であり、１９７０年代以降は年間数十億ドルの軍事支援を提供してきた。だが、民主・共和両党に熱心に働きかけてきた歴代の指導者とは異なり、ネタニヤフ氏はあからさまに共和党を支持してきた。

民主党と一部の共和党の間でのイスラエル支持は、イスラエルが２０２３年のイスラム組織ハマスによる攻撃を受けてガザで軍事攻撃に乗り出した後に揺らぎ、今年に入ってトランプ氏とネタニヤフ氏がイランへの共同攻撃を命じて以来、その支持はさらに低下した。

イスラエルの中道左派野党「民主党」のヤイル・ゴラン党首はＸへの投稿で、米中間選挙の結果は「ネタニヤフ氏が民主・共和両党の間でいかに有害な存在かを浮き彫りにしている」と指摘した。 

中道野党イェシュアティドのラピド党首は、この結果は、ネタニヤフ氏が政権にとどまることを「イスラエルは許容できない」ことを示していると述べ、「それはわれわれの安全保障を脅かし、民主主義を危険にさらし、国際舞台でのわれわれの立場を損なうことになる」と強調した。

米中間選挙のわずか１週間前に実施されたイスラエル総選挙では、ネタニヤフ首相の陣営がユダヤ系国民から事前の予想を上回る支持を獲得した。ネタニヤフ氏の陣営は予想通り国会で過半数を失ったものの、最大の対抗馬であるガディ・アイゼンコット氏が同氏を退陣に追い込むための明確な道筋を阻むには十分な結果を残した。

アイゼンコット氏は４日、Ｘへの投稿で、自身の指導下でイスラエルは米政府との関係を修復すると表明。「われわれはこのパートナーシップを刷新・深化させ、長年にわたり依拠してきた超党派的な基盤を強化し、中東全体の前進に向けて取り組む」と述べた。

イスラエルのヘルツォグ大統領は、４日と５日に各党代表と協議した上で、両氏のいずれかに次期政権の組閣を委ねる見通し。その間、ネタニヤフ氏は暫定首相として職務にとどまる。

ネタニヤフ氏はこれまでのところ、米選挙の結果について沈黙を保っている。同氏の事務所はコメント要請に応じなかった。

items.title: イラン、米中間選挙を「反戦の審判」と歓迎　警戒態勢は継続
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Parisa Hafezi

[４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Parisa Hafezi

[４日 ロイター] - イラン政府は、米中間選挙でトランプ大統領に下された手厳しい審判を歓迎し、有権者が同大統領の始めた戦争を拒絶したと宣言した。一方で、同国は攻撃が再開される可能性に備え、高度な警戒態勢を維持している。

イランの首席交渉官であるガリバフ国会議長はＸへの投稿で、「良心のためか生活費のためかはともかく、米国民は『戦争にノー』と言った。われわれはこのメッセージを支持する」と表明。米政府はイランを再び攻撃することで世論を無視すべきではないと述べた。

イランの最高指導者モジタバ師は文書による声明で、どの政党が政権を握ろうと米国の敵意は続くとし、米国への「わずかな服従の傾向さえ」示すことに警告を発した。その上で、「米国は自らの覇権の終わりを遠いものと見ているが、われわれは近いと見ている」と付け加えた。

イランの保守系紙ジャメジャムは、選挙結果を「トランプ主義の黄昏（たそがれ）」と評した。

３日投開票の米中間選挙では、民主党が上下両院の過半数を奪還した。共和党の地盤での民主党の勝利は、トランプ氏の経済運営や、ガソリン価格を押し上げた開戦の決断に対する深い不満を浮き彫りにした。

イランでは、司法府が運営する報道機関がＸ上で広まっているジョークを紹介。「トランプ氏はイランでの体制転換には失敗したが、テキサスでは成功した」というもので、南部テキサス州で数十年ぶりに民主党が上院選に勝利したことを指している。

ただ、イラン高官２人はロイターに対し、イランの指導部は民主党の勝利を歓迎しているものの、トランプ氏がその埋め合わせに軍事攻撃に踏み切る可能性をイランは懸念しており、高度な警戒態勢を続けていると語った。

選挙後にイラン戦争が再燃しかねないとの懸念の中、仲介役は紛争終結に向けた取り組みを強化している。しかしトランプ氏は３日、投票後の戦闘作戦再開の可能性を排除しなかった。イランも戦争が再開すれば、より広範な報復を計画している。

トランプ氏はＦＯＸニュースのインタビューで、中間選挙で共和党が敗北した一因がイラン戦争だったと認めた。
